text:
michelle: Quick follow-up on the Dedicated GPU pool autoscale RFC — thinking about the interface between the global scaler and per-tenant admission controller. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and a tiny API sketch so we can iterate.

michelle: Proposal (very rough):
```
capacity_intent:
  min_replicas: 2
  headroom_pct: 20    # keep 20% free GPU slots for latency SLOs
  burst_credit: 500   # tenant-level burst budget
  priority_class: prod|staging|batch
  latency_slo_ms: 200
```

michelle: The questions: should the "global scaler" own headroom calculations and credits, or should it just expose raw capacity and let "admission" do the math?

raj: my 2c — separate responsibilities makes sense. global scaler should only publish cluster intent and available capacity windows. admission controller should enforce tenant-level policies (credits, preemption). That prevents double-binding.

raj: downside: admission needs accurate near-real-time view of pending scale operations. that gets tricky if we have eventual consistency in the control plane.

olivia: we need metrics to make admission decisions: p95 latency per-tenant, request queue length, active KV-cache pressure. If admission has to compute headroom it will need these signals. Is that duplicating logic?

sam: maybe split into two APIs: 1) capacity_snapshot (read-only, frequent) 2) scale_intent (write-only, slower). capacity_snapshot is the thing global scaler publishes every ~10s, containing total_gpus, reserved_for_priority, estimated_headroom. admission queries that.

sam: sketch:
```
capacity_snapshot:
  ts: 1852109876
  total_gpus: 128
  reserved: { prod: 60, staging: 10 }
  estimated_headroom_slots: 20
```

julia: +1 to the two-API approach. Also: we should be explicit about failure modes. If capacity_snapshot lags, admission must conservatively reject bursts for safety. If scale_intent is too chatty it could thrash the autoscaler. Rate limits needed.

michelle: good call. Tradeoff I'm worried about: if admission makes conservative rejections, UX for end-users (PLG customers) degrades. We could allow best-effort soft-accepts where requests are admitted if tenant has burst_credit > 0 even if headroom unknown. then admission decrements credit and emits compensating scale_intent. Needs atomicity guarantees?

raj: atomicity across controllers is hard. I'd prefer a lease model: admission obtains a short-lived slot lease from global scaler (like token bucket) and consumes that locally. lease acquisition is cheaper than asking for an immediate scale operation.

olivia: lease model sounds clean. We need to model cost accounting: who pays for prewarmed GPUs? tenant budgets or platform? That affects priority_class semantics.

sam: implementation note: keep the lease protocol simple gRPC + protobuf. fields: tenant_id, slots_requested, ttl_ms, can_preempt (bool). Autoscaler returns granted_slots and a lease_id. Admission uses lease_id to attach to allocations.

michelle: timeline question: do we want to prototype this as a daemonset + central controller, or as extension controllers (CRDs) in our control plane? My vote: prototype as daemon + feature flag, then convert to CRD once API shape stabilizes.

julia: prototype as daemon is faster, but we should design the daemon to be a thin shim that can be swapped for CRD-backed controller. keep schema stable.

autoscaler-bot: [simulated] scale_intent accepted: 40 -> adding 2 nodes (GPU type A100) (eta 45s)

raj: another edge: cross-region fallback. If pool in region A is saturated, admission could choose to route to region B (higher latency). We need region-aware capacity_snapshot and a routing hint in the lease response.

olivia: ops concern: how do we debug rejections? add a short human-readable rejection_reason and attach the recent capacity_snapshot id to the response. log traces into Console UI for customers.

michelle: action items I hear: 1) sam to prototype capacity_snapshot + lease proto (daemon) — 2w spike. 2) raj + olivia to write test matrix for failure modes (laggy snapshots, preemption, region fallback). 3) julia to draft migration plan for daemon -> CRD. 4) michelle to update RFC with API sketch and tradeoffs.

michelle: any objections or things I missed?

sam: no objections. will start proto and post links to repo by EOD.

raj: will take test matrix item.

olivia: will draft observability hooks (Console traces + SLO dashboards).

julia: I'll start the migration plan doc.

michelle: sweet. putting this in the follow-up ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2431 — thanks all :thumbsup:
